name: Zoe Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have answered calls and chats at the contact centre for years. I finished secondary school, earn the usual rate, and keep up with the average queue. I use an AI draft now and then after someone else has tested it, but I check the invoice before sending anything.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Idris, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. He works at a plant nursery. We have about five months of expenses saved, and some other centres are within reach. I like the small moment when a customer understands the charge on a bill. I do not like when a tidy script hides an earlier promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau sounds like the draft helper I sometimes use for a simple invoice reply. I would keep the old customer promise visible beside the new draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job keeps going, and five months saved makes a house repair possible without panic. I still would not treat that money as spare while the mortgage comes due.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep my normal calls and check any draft against the full invoice history. In the first year of small change, I’d add a fixed part of each pay to our house reserve before planning a holiday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm enough about work, watchful about the household. A customer’s old payment promise should not vanish because a new reply looks cleaner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old promise would a draft miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once found a promised fee reversal buried in a chat from the week before. The first draft missed it, so I checked the record and sent the customer the correct date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you spend the reserve on a holiday?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Idris (my partner) and I would keep five months set aside for bills and repairs. We can talk about a holiday after the reserve grows, not before.

say: I’d call the **draft helper** useful for simple invoices.
I’d keep **old customer promises** visible before sending replies.
think: I think my **job continues** under small AI change.
I would protect the **five-month reserve** from ordinary spending.
do: Keep **normal calls** and check full invoice histories in 2026.
Add a **fixed amount** to house savings in the first year.
S0.quote: A customer’s old payment promise should not vanish because a new reply looks cleaner.
fieldNote: Her **five-month cushion** helps with repairs but remains earmarked.
She uses AI **occasionally** only after checking the record.
A missed **fee reversal** shapes her caution.

steps.text: Keep answering calls and checking drafts against full invoice histories
Add a fixed amount from each pay to the house reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption may take simple invoice answers first, and I want the error rate shown before our rota changes. I would ask whether agents can still correct a promise the tool missed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think some of my ordinary chats may disappear, even if harder billing calls remain. Five months saved helps me compare offers, but Idris’s nursery pay alone would not cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for a paid trial of the new answer tool and test twelve old promised refunds against it if errors can be recorded. In the first year simple chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid billing role at another centre only if the offered wage and weekly hours cover our mortgage, keeping my shifts until a signed offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but able to test a real sample. I will learn a tool after it proves useful, not because its name sounds clever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trial count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would count how many promises the tool missed and take the list to my supervisor. One bad reply can become two calls if nobody reads the earlier chat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which wage figure would matter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Idris (my partner) to compare the whole week of offered pay with our mortgage bill. A higher hourly rate can still mean a smaller pay packet.

say: I’d ask for **error rates** on missed promises before the centre changes our rota.
I’d defend a way to **correct missed promises**.
think: I think my **ordinary chats** may shrink.
I know Idris’s **nursery wage** cannot cover our mortgage alone.
I would keep our **current shifts** until a signed offer arrives.
do: Test **twelve old refunds** on paid time with recordable errors in 2026.
Seek **posted billing work** only with offered mortgage-covering wages and weekly hours; keep current shifts until a signed offer arrives.
S1.quote: A higher hourly rate can still mean a smaller pay packet.
fieldNote: She tests **old promises**, not only generated wording.
She compares **weekly pay** before switching centres.
The trial must allow **error recording** on paid time.
She needs **whole-week income**, not a better-sounding hourly rate.

steps.text: Test twelve old refund promises with the new tool on paid time if errors are recordable
Apply for posted paid billing work only with offered weekly wage and hours covering mortgage
Keep current paid calls until a signed mortgage-covering offer arrives

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could answer and check even complicated calls. I would ask for written notice and posted paid jobs before a rota change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could remove most of my screen work in 2028. Robots around 2031 come later, so they do not lengthen my call job; five months saved is a buffer, not a new wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d pause the planned garden path and ask for the written staffing date. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception job only if its offered wage and weekly hours cover our mortgage, and take employer-funded training on paid time only if that vacancy requires it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, though I have a few months to look. Five months of savings cannot replace a customer-service wage forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say about the path?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Idris (my partner) we can use the old path if it is safe. I would rather keep the repair money for the mortgage than lay new stones this year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What training terms would you accept?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the posted job, starting hours and who pays for the course. Without those terms I would keep searching, not buy a certificate on hope.

say: I’d ask management for **written notice** before any 2028 call cuts.
I’d seek **posted paid jobs** with real weekly hours.
think: I think AGI could remove **most screen work** in 2028.
I know **2031 robots** give a headset no extra time.
do: Defer the **garden path** if safe and request staffing dates in 2026.
Apply for **posted reception work** after 2028 with offered mortgage-covering wage and weekly hours.
Take **funded training** on paid time only if required for that named posted paid vacancy.
S2.quote: Five months of savings cannot replace a customer-service wage forever.
fieldNote: She plans around **2028 thinking AI** for calls.
The **path delay** depends on it being safe.
Training requires **employer funding** and paid time for a posted role.

steps.text: Delay laying a new garden path only while the old path remains safe
Apply for posted paid reception work with mortgage-covering offered wage and weekly hours
Take funded training on paid time only if required for the named posted paid vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives a few years to see whether billing review is a real paid job. I would ask for the posted wage and training plan before committing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn review work in five years if the centre funds a course and pays for the hours. Full AGI might still do review tasks, so I would not call the job permanent shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded billing-review course on paid time only if a posted paid vacancy requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written wage and weekly hours cover our mortgage, keeping my current calls until a signed offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I have time to look at actual work. A course tied to a paid billing-review vacancy is a bridge; an unposted certificate is a bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the reviewer show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask a reviewer to show me three cases where the old customer promise changed the answer. I need to know whether the job is more than reading what a tool already wrote.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Idris check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Idris (my partner) the full-week wage and the hours I must work. We would not spend the reserve on a certificate with no job.

say: I’d ask for **posted review wages** before anyone starts a new course.
I’d request a **paid learning plan** tied to vacancies.
think: I think I could learn **billing review** with funded time.
I know **AGI may reach review** work too.
do: Take a **funded paid-time review course** only for a posted vacancy.
Apply after 2031 for **posted paid review** with written mortgage-covering weekly wages and hours; keep calls until a signed offer.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to test the work.
S3.quote: A course tied to a paid billing-review vacancy is a bridge; an unposted certificate is a bill.
fieldNote: She wants **three real cases** before trusting the role.
The course needs **funding and paid time** for a posted vacancy.
The offer must preserve **weekly mortgage pay**.

steps.text: Take funded billing-review course on paid time only for a posted paid vacancy
Apply for posted review work with written weekly wage and hours covering mortgage after 2031
Keep current paid calls until a signed mortgage-covering offer arrives

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to compare real posted work while we keep earning. I would ask the centre for yearly paid-hour figures so a slow cut is visible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep my usual wage for years and save more, though full thinking AI could still take calls in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later; the mortgage is due all along.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and add a fixed part of each pay to savings. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid billing work only if my call hours fall and the written wage and weekly hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, okay about the next year. A decade before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without pretending the mortgage stops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which number belongs in the yearly report?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for paid agent hours, not just customers answered. A smaller human rota can look like success if the report only counts chats.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Idris (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a workable route. We can look at nearby centres first.

say: I’d ask for **yearly paid-agent hours**, not just answered customer counts.
I’d say families need **real posted work** before changing fields.
think: I think I could **earn and save** for years.
I know **2036 thinking AI** could still take calls.
do: Keep **taking calls** and save from each pay.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2036 if hours fall and weekly pay covers mortgage.
feel: **Uneasy** about later work, okay about next year.
S4.quote: A decade before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without pretending the mortgage stops.
fieldNote: She tracks **paid hours**, not only answered chats.
A move requires a **signed offer** and school route.
She would check **nearby centres** before moving the family.

steps.text: Keep answering customer calls while the centre staffs them
Put a fixed part of each pay into mortgage savings
Apply for posted billing work if hours fall and written weekly wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The thinking work on our calls could move before I have time to test a paid alternative. Five months saved buys us a search, but I would need written notice and a posted paid role whose actual weekly hours and wage cover the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who notices a promise that was made last week. A customer remembers last week’s payment promise even when a new script pretends it was never written.

headlineQuote: A customer remembers last week’s payment promise even when a new script pretends it was never written.
portrait: At **43**, Zoe is an experienced average-skill agent after secondary school on typical pay.
She and Idris support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with five months saved.
She uses AI **occasionally** after colleagues show it works, checking invoices herself.
She tests **paid alternatives** before changing work and protects weekly mortgage income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end call work before a tested paid alternative is ready.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** and a posted paid job with mortgage-covering weekly hours would help.
